intro: These four skills sit at the edges of the conditionals. The first asks which 'if' survives when the sentence ends in a request or a plan. The second turns 'if' against reality: what you wish had happened, or wish were true. The third flips the logic to 'even if': B holds whether or not A happens. The last covers the N2 forms that frame A as a mere supposition (としたら, とすれば), a hard-to-reach possibility (ものなら), or the one thing that would change B (ない限り).

skills.rule: If B is a request, invitation, wish or plan, と is never allowed, ば only after a state, and たら or なら carry the sentence.
skills.explain:
Look at the end of the sentence first. If it expresses the speaker's will (〜てください, 〜ましょう, 〜ませんか, 〜たい, 〜つもり, 〜なさい, 〜ほうがいい), the conditional choice narrows at once.

と is out: it only links A to results that follow by themselves. ば is allowed when A is a state: an adjective, ある, いる, a potential form, a negative (時間があれば手伝って, 安ければ買いたい). When A is an action verb, a request after ば is wrong (着けば電話して ✗), and a plan sounds natural only when someone else does A (田中さんが行けば、私も行きます).

That leaves たら and なら. たら: A happens first, then B (着いたら電話して). なら: A is a premise or a plan, and B is advice or a decision about it, often done before A (行くなら、切符を早めに買おう).

examples.jp: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
examples.en: Please call me when you get to the station.

examples.jp: 時間[じかん]があれ{ば}、手伝[てつだ]ってください。
examples.en: If you have time, please help me.

examples.jp: 暇[ひま]だっ{たら}、一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]ませんか。
examples.en: If you're free, shall we watch a film together?

examples.jp: 安[やす]けれ{ば}、二[ふた]つ買[か]いたいです。
examples.en: If they're cheap, I'd like to buy two.

examples.jp: 仕事[しごと]が終[お]わっ{たら}、飲[の]みに行[い]こう。
examples.en: Let's go for a drink once work is over.

examples.jp: 旅行[りょこう]に行[い]く{なら}、早[はや]めに切符[きっぷ]を買[か]いましょう。
examples.en: If we're going on a trip, let's buy the tickets early.

contrast.note: と cannot introduce anything the speaker wants or asks for: 着くと電話して is wrong. と belongs to automatic results: 着くと、いつも雨が降る.
With a state in A, ば takes a request (時間があれば来て). With an action verb in A it does not: 着けば電話して is wrong, 着いたら電話して is right.
たら asks for B after A. なら gives advice about a plan: 来たら連絡して (once you are here), 来るなら連絡して (if you plan to come, tell me before).

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]く{と}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。

mistakes.bad: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]け{ば}、連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.good: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]い{たら}、連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.note: The same person arrives and then gets in touch: an action verb with ば cannot lead into a request; たら can.

skills.tip: Will or request at the end? Cross out と. Action verb before ば? Cross out ば. Then: A first, たら; advice on a plan, なら.

skills.rule: 〜ばよかった (or 〜たらよかった) is 'I wish I had'; add のに to complain, and use 〜ばいいのに / 〜たらいいのに for 'I wish it were so'.
skills.explain:
Regret about the past: put the thing you did not do into ば or たら and end with よかった: もっと勉強すればよかった 'I should have studied more'. Adding のに turns it outward or makes it a sigh: 言ってくれればよかったのに 'you could have told me'. The negative is 〜なければよかった 'I wish I hadn't'.

An unreal condition, the opposite of what actually happened, is A-ば/たら followed by a result and のに: 時間があれば手伝えたのに 'if I'd had time I could have helped (but I didn't)'. For a completed past situation, ていれば / ていたら is clearest: 知っていたら教えたのに.

A wish about now or the future that you doubt will come true: 〜ばいいのに / 〜たらいいのに. と never forms regret, and neither does a verb + なら (するならよかった ✗). After a noun or な-adjective, なら is simply the ば-form of だ and works: 休みならよかったのに. ても is concession, not regret.
patterns: [ば-form] よかった / [た-form]ら よかった
[ば / たら clause]、[past result] のに
[ば-form] いいのに / [た-form]ら いいのに

examples.jp: もっと勉強[べんきょう]すれ{ばよかった}。
examples.en: I wish I had studied more.

examples.jp: 傘[かさ]を持[も]って来[く]れ{ばよかった}。
examples.en: I should have brought an umbrella.

examples.jp: 早[はや]く言[い]ってくれ{たらよかったのに}。
examples.en: You could have told me sooner.

examples.jp: 時間[じかん]があれ{ば}、手伝[てつだ]えた{のに}。
examples.en: If I'd had the time, I could have helped.

examples.jp: もう少[すこ]し背[せ]が高[たか]けれ{ばいいのに}。
examples.en: I wish I were a little taller.

examples.jp: あんなこと、言[い]わなけれ{ばよかった}。
examples.en: I wish I hadn't said that.

contrast.note: ても reports that A did not change B: 勉強しても受からなかった 'I studied but still failed'. ばよかった says A did not happen and should have.
With verbs, regret is built only on ば or たら: 勉強するとよかった and 勉強するならよかった are wrong. After a noun or な-adjective, なら works as the ば-form of だ: 日曜日ならよかったのに.

mistakes.bad: もっと練習[れんしゅう]する{とよかった}。
mistakes.good: もっと練習[れんしゅう]すれ{ばよかった}。
mistakes.note: 'I should have' is ばよかった (or したらよかった), never とよかった.

mistakes.bad: 知[し]っ{たら}、教[おし]えました。
mistakes.good: 知[し]ってい{たら}、教[おし]えた{のに}。
mistakes.note: 知ったら教えました reads as a real past sequence ('when I found out, I told them'); 'if I had known' needs ていたら and のに.

skills.tip: Can you say 'I wish' or 'should have'? Reach for ば or たら, then よかった or いいのに. のに at the end means 'but it didn't happen'.

skills.rule: A ても B: B holds even if A, so the result you would expect from A does not follow; nouns and な-adjectives take でも.
skills.explain:
ても is the て-form plus も: 行っても, 飲んでも, 高くても, 静かでも, 雨でも. It cancels the link that たら or ば would make. 雨が降ったら中止です: rain leads to cancellation. 雨が降っても行います: rain changes nothing.

It works for hypotheses (even if it rains tomorrow) and for real past events (I took the medicine, but the fever didn't go down). たとえ at the start strengthens 'even if'. With a question word it means 'no matter': いくら, どんなに, 何回, 誰が ... ても.

The main clause often holds a negative or an unchanged plan, because that is what 'even if' produces. Form check: い-adjectives drop い and take くても (高くても, not 高いでも); いい becomes よくても.
patterns: いくら / どんなに [て-form]も、[B]

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っ{ても}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]います。
examples.en: Even if it rains, the match will go ahead.

examples.jp: 高[たか]く{ても}、このかばんを買[か]います。
examples.en: I'm buying this bag even if it's expensive.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]は日曜日[にちようび]{でも}、会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]きます。
examples.en: Even though tomorrow is Sunday, I'm going to the office.

examples.jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]ん{でも}、熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がりませんでした。
examples.en: Even after I took the medicine, my fever didn't go down.

examples.jp: いくら練習[れんしゅう]し{ても}、上手[じょうず]になりません。
examples.en: No matter how much I practise, I don't get any better.

examples.jp: たとえ反対[はんたい]され{ても}、留学[りゅうがく]するつもりです。
examples.en: Even if people oppose it, I intend to study abroad.

contrast.note: たら makes A lead to B: 高かったら買わない. ても says A makes no difference: 高くても買う. Choosing たら reverses the logic.
ば sets A as the requirement for B (安ければ買う). ても denies that A matters. いくら / どんなに go with ても, not ば.
のに is only for a real fact plus disappointment (飲んだのに治らない). ても also covers the hypothetical and carries no complaint.

mistakes.bad: 高[たか]かっ{たら}、買[か]います。
mistakes.good: 高[たか]く{ても}、買[か]います。
mistakes.note: 'Even if it's expensive' needs ても; たら means 'if it's expensive, I'll buy it'.

mistakes.bad: いくら呼[よ]ん{だら}、返事[へんじ]がない。
mistakes.good: いくら呼[よ]ん{でも}、返事[へんじ]がない。
mistakes.note: 'No matter how' is いくら … ても.

mistakes.bad: 静[しず]か{くても}、眠[ねむ]れません。
mistakes.good: 静[しず]か{でも}、眠[ねむ]れません。
mistakes.note: な-adjectives and nouns take でも, not くても.

skills.tip: Put 'even' in front of the English 'if'. If B stays the same whatever A does, it is ても.

skills.rule: としたら / とすれば: 'supposing that'; ものなら: 'if it were at all possible' (potential form) or 'if you dared' (volitional form); ない限り: 'unless', B holds as long as A does not happen.
skills.explain:
としたら and とすれば follow the plain form, with だ after nouns (本当だとしたら). A is a supposition the speaker does not know to be true or treats as imaginary: 宝くじが当たったとしたら. B is a question, guess or evaluation. とすれば sounds more logical and written; とすると is close.

ものなら attaches to the potential form for something you can hardly achieve: 戻れるものなら戻りたい 'if only I could go back'; B is a wish or a dare (やれるものならやってみろ). After the volitional form (〜ようものなら) it means 'if you so much as did A', and B is a bad outcome.

ない限り means B continues unless A happens: 謝らない限り許さない. B is usually a lasting state or a refusal. It is stronger than なければ and suits rules and conditions.
patterns: [plain form / noun だ] としたら / とすれば、[question / guess]

examples.jp: 宝[たから]くじが当[あ]たった{としたら}、何[なに]に使[つか]いますか。
examples.en: Supposing you won the lottery, what would you spend it on?

examples.jp: その話[はなし]が本当[ほんとう]だ{とすれば}、大変[たいへん]なことになる。
examples.en: If that story is true, we're in serious trouble.

examples.jp: 戻[もど]れる{ものなら}、学生[がくせい]時代[じだい]に戻[もど]りたい。
examples.en: If only I could, I'd go back to my student days.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]に嘘[うそ]をつこう{ものなら}、ひどく叱[しか]られる。
examples.en: If I so much as told my father a lie, I'd be scolded terribly.

examples.jp: 本人[ほんにん]が来[こ]{ない限[かぎ]り}、手続[てつづ]きはできません。
examples.en: Unless the person themselves comes, the procedure can't be done.

examples.jp: よほどのことが{ない限[かぎ]り}、明日[あした]の会議[かいぎ]には出[で]ます。
examples.en: Unless something serious comes up, I'll attend tomorrow's meeting.

contrast.note: たら treats A as an event that may come: 着いたら電話して. としたら treats it as a supposition to reason from, so it suits questions and guesses, not plans or requests about real events.
なければ is a plain 'if not'. ない限り insists that only A would change B, so it suits rules: 許可がない限り入れない.

contrast.vs: ものなら / ようものなら
contrast.note: Potential + ものなら is a wish for the near impossible. Volitional + ものなら is a warning of what any attempt would bring.

mistakes.bad: 行[い]く{ものなら}、行[い]きたい。
mistakes.good: 行[い]ける{ものなら}、行[い]きたい。
mistakes.note: ものなら in the 'if only I could' sense needs the potential form.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]いた{としたら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.note: A real, expected arrival with a request takes たら; としたら is for suppositions.

skills.tip: 'Supposing ...?' としたら. 'If only I could' ものなら. 'Unless ... never' ない限り.
